//: lddb-demo Realtime Database rules — the course and student catalogue.
Deploy with:   firebase deploy --only database --project lddb-demo
(or paste into Firebase console -> Realtime Database -> Rules)
This database is currently wide open, which is the single most urgent thing
these rules fix: today anyone who views the page source can rewrite every
course, faculty name and student record in it.
The shape it needs is unusual, so it is worth stating plainly:
READ is public and unauthenticated. It has to be. Browsing courses, picking
a subject and downloading a cover page PDF are free features that work with
no account — that was a deliberate product decision, and it means the course
list must be readable by a visitor who has never signed in. None of it is
sensitive: it is a university's public course catalogue.
WRITE requires a `coverAdmin` claim. Students never sign in to THIS project
at all — they sign in to LabDDB-Pro. So a normal `auth != null` check would
be useless here (there is no normal user to match) and an email allowlist
would need this project to own the sign-in. Instead, the coverpage admin
signs in to LabDDB-Pro with Google, the Worker checks their `coverAdmin`
role, and mints a short-lived custom token for lddb-demo carrying that claim
(POST /api/cover-token -> lib/api.js). The claim below is what that token
puts in `auth.token`. A one-hour token, minted only for accounts the project
admin has granted the role, is what stands between the catalogue and the
open internet.
`students` is the exception to public read. Roll numbers and names are
personal data, and the generators only ever look up one roll at a time by
exact key — which stays possible under a per-record read rule while a bulk
scrape of the whole node does not. The admin panel's student list reads the
node whole, so that read needs the coverAdmin claim too.
The generators write nothing here, so there is no client write path to keep
working. Only admin.html writes, and only through the custom token.

cvr3_courses.//: Public course catalogue: codes, titles, faculty, assignments, experiments.

cvr3_meta.//: Counters and settings shown on the admin dashboard.

//: Name/roll lookups. The generators read one record at a time by exact key
(students/<roll>), which the per-record rule allows anonymously. Reading the
whole node — which is what a scrape would do, and what the admin panel's
student list legitimately does — needs the coverAdmin claim.
